summary.headline: Home First Q4 FY26: record Q4 disbursement of INR1,572 crore (+23.5% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR540 crore (+41.4% YoY); FY27 AUM growth guided ~25%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 saw record quarterly disbursement, PAT of INR149 crore (+42.7% YoY, +6.6% QoQ), and AUM of INR15,878 crore (+24.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ). Asset quality improved sequentially, with 30+ DPD down 50bps to 3.2% and gross Stage 3 down 20bps to 1.8%. Management attributed the H1 weakness to elevated delinquencies, tariff impacts, and internal staffing gaps, which it says have since been resolved. Management guided to ~25% AUM growth in FY27, a 5%-5.25% spread and 30-40bps credit cost, and said there is no visible impact yet from the Middle East conflict.

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / book value per share

financial_highlights.change: Stage 3 provision cover 24% vs 22% in Dec'25
FY26 co-lending disbursement INR307 crore vs INR153 crore in FY25

segments.name: Individual housing loans / LAP mix
segments.commentary: Individual housing is 83% of origination share; management guides to an ~80:20 housing-to-LAP mix going forward, with LAP yields around 14-14.5% and a 100-150bps yield gap versus housing.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Co-lending book INR593 crore (3.7% of AUM); co-lending is largely INR20-40 lakh tickets and yields 8-10%, with management expecting normal run-rate from June after April-May issues are resolved.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Gujarat, MP and Rajasthan show healthy growth and stable asset quality; Maharashtra (Mumbai, Pune) has regained momentum; Tamil Nadu and Telangana were weak on internal team issues; Karnataka steady apart from e-Khata blip; UP team being built for FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of around 25% YoY, with the company citing exit momentum and April disbursements.
Spread (excl. co-lending) to be held in a 5%-5.25% range, with pass-through of borrowing cost changes to customers in both directions.
Credit cost guided at 30-40bps for FY27, unchanged from the prior guidance.
Opex-to-assets expected to stay range-bound at 2.6%-2.7%.
Cost of borrowing in Q1 FY27 expected to be broadly at Q4 levels; no PLR change planned in the next quarter.
Plans to add 30-40 branches a year, with employees per branch kept in a 9-12 range.
capex_capacity: Network at 171 branches and 373 touch points after adding 6 branches and 5 touch points in Q4.
Headcount 1,855 after net 221 additions in FY26, mostly customer-facing.
Branch strategy: open only where potential is INR2-3 crore monthly disbursement; about 50 branches currently below INR50 crore annual disbursement and about 10 below INR10 crore.
Green homes: 140 homes certified in Q4, cumulative 450 as of Mar'26.
AI: proprietary agents live for income assessment and bank statement analysis; lead qualification, legal/technical evaluation and bureau analysis in pilot.
demand_pricing: Origination yield 13% in Q4 (average, exit rate similar, +/-2bps); portfolio yield excl. co-lending 13.2%; yield range 12-14% across products.
Pricing is algorithm-driven and centrally set; limited month-to-month variation.
Demand improved from October onwards per management; no demand drop seen from the West Asia conflict; April 2026 collections and fresh slippage better than April 2025 and April 2024.
Competition: no new significant competitors in the southern states; large HFCs not seen targeting its ZIP codes.
Connector fee negotiations ongoing; overall commission movement of 10-15bps typical, offset by faster turnaround and timely payouts.

qa_highlights.question: Was H1 FY26 weakness demand-led, and is demand and credit now improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited elevated delinquencies, tariff impacts, collection difficulty and internal staffing gaps; demand improved from October and credit and collections have improved since.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 AUM growth of 25% be sustained, and how are distribution and new states being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to rebuilt senior leadership, improved channel proposition (turnaround, product bouquet, co-lending), a jump in connector numbers, and Mumbai/Pune success; expects the trend to continue for 2-3 years if all goes well.

qa_highlights.question: Will rates hardening affect pricing and the spread?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 borrowing cost expected broadly flat; repricing beyond Q1 undecided; spread above 5% is the guided floor and the company is confident of maintaining 5%-5.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-of-funds gap between balance sheet and co-lending, and versus large AAA-rated HFCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending funding is less than 20bps different from balance sheet borrowing; the gap to large AAA HFCs is 40bps, at most 50bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving into prime lending as larger HFCs enter affordable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target customer is the same informal-income affordable customer; prime customers borrow at 7.25-8%, while co-lending is priced at 8-10% and core affordable at 12.5-13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the write-off figure and auction volume?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 write-offs about INR36 crore, in line with business growth; auctions of 50-100 units a month, about 1,000 units for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth reach 30% over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 25% guidance and said it is difficult to say whether 30% is achievable.

risks_watch: Rising interest rates: repricing decision beyond Q1 FY27 undecided; spread could compress if borrowing costs rise and repricing lags.
Co-lending volumes were low in Q4 due to regulatory-related issues; full normalisation is expected only from June 2026.
Middle East conflict: no impact seen yet, but management acknowledges sporadic anecdotal concerns.
Attrition and staffing: employees per branch to remain in a 9-12 range; Tamil Nadu and Telangana recovery depends on team build-out.
Write-offs rising in absolute terms (~INR36 crore) with auctions of about 1,000 units a year.
Competitive intensity from larger HFCs and banks in ticket sizes above INR15 lakh and in developer-led Mumbai/Pune markets.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and profitability, with specific numbers provided across the call. Cautious on rate direction beyond Q1 FY27, where management said repricing decisions are not available today, and evasive on the 30% AUM growth question, which it said was difficult to predict.

growth.why: Management guides ~25% AUM growth in FY27, backed by exit momentum, April disbursements, and a 30-40 branch-per-year rollout, with no specific capacity or order-book numbers beyond branch additions; Q4 AUM +24.9% YoY and total income +21.3% YoY support the case.
